listenings.text: Thank you for applying. This message explains what is going to happen next, so that nobody has to write and ask. In two weeks we are going to send you an email confirming that your file is complete. If a document is missing, that email is going to say which one, and you are going to have ten days to send it. In November we are going to invite about sixty candidates to an interview. The interview is thirty minutes long, it is in English, and it is not a test of your accent. We want to hear how you think about a problem. Final answers go out in January. One last thing, and it is important. We are not going to read your motivation letter as literature. We are going to read it for one thing: why this program, and why now.

Everybody in this market is looking at the same calendar right now. The harvest in Mato Grosso is going to start in about eight weeks, and when it starts, roughly forty million tons are going to move toward three ports in ninety days. Nothing about that is a surprise. It happens every year. What changes is the plan. A trader who books freight in June is going to pay one price. A trader who waits until the trucks are already on the road is going to pay another one, and he is going to blame the market, not the calendar. So here is the question I ask every client in April, and it is not a clever question. What are you going to do in September, and who else in your office knows about it? If nobody can answer that, there is no plan. There is only hope.
